title: Dominican Republic Formally Commits $20 Million to UN Gang Suppression Force Trust Fund
detail: In a formal diplomatic communication to the United Nations in New York, Dominican Foreign Minister Roberto Alvarez officially confirmed the Dominican Republic's $20 million financial commitment to the UN Multi-Partner Trust Fund supporting the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) in Haiti. The contribution is structured over two fiscal years: $10 million in 2026 and $10 million in 2027. The Dominican Republic's pledge is notable given the DR's historically complex relationship with Haiti — including a 2023 border wall construction, ongoing deportation tensions, and repeated border closures — and reflects the DR's growing recognition that Haitian instability directly threatens regional security and Dominican economic interests. The DR commitment adds to the over $220 million pledged from 13+ states as reported at the April 23, 2026 UN Security Council briefing, with $59 million disbursed to date. Qatar had separately pledged $30 million. The GSF currently has approximately 545 advance troops deployed in Port-au-Prince (400 Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran) following Kenya's final MSS officer departure on April 28, 2026. National pledges for the full 5,500-authorized-ceiling force now exceed the ceiling, with full operational capacity expected by fall–end 2026.

title: Saint-Marc Imposes Nightly Curfew as Gang Insecurity Expands in Artibonite
detail: The municipality of Saint-Marc, a strategic port city in the Artibonite Department approximately 80 km north of Port-au-Prince, imposed a nightly security curfew effective May 5, 2026, prohibiting all vehicle and motorcycle circulation from 8:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Municipal authorities cited deteriorating security conditions driven by gang expansion from deeper in the Artibonite region toward the coastal city. Saint-Marc is a critical transit point for goods and fuel moving between Cap-Haïtien and Port-au-Prince on Route Nationale 1, and its destabilization would further fragment already precarious supply chains serving the capital and northern Haiti. The curfew follows the Gran Grif gang's March 28–April 6 offensive across the Artibonite Valley, which generated over 13,000 additional displaced persons, the March 30 Jean-Denis massacre (16–70 killed), and a subsequent advance by Gran Grif and Kokorat San Ras gangs to within 19 km of Gonaïves. The broader pattern of gang expansion beyond Port-au-Prince into agricultural and transit zones represents a structural escalation that the GSF advance contingent of approximately 545 troops — entirely focused on Port-au-Prince operations — is not yet large enough to address simultaneously.

media.caption: Saint-Marc, Artibonite imposes nightly curfew banning vehicle and motorcycle traffic from 8:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. due to deteriorating gang security
